newsitem.title: USA: U.S. equity funds rise 2.61 pct in Q3 - Lipper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. equity funds rise 2.61 pct in Q3 - Lipper.

text.p: Returns of U.S. equity mutual funds increased 2.61 percent in the third quarter, despite a dismal July in which the average fund declined by 6.08 percent, according to Lipper Analytical Services Inc.
The top performing sector was financial services, which gained 7.64 percent in the quarter.

"Mergers and acqusitions among some leading banks sparked the biggest gains," Lipper said in a statement. Lipper cited Chase Manhattan Corp rising after it closed its merger with Chemical Bank and NationsBank Corp's agreement to buy Boatmen's Boatmen's Bancshares Inc.
Total return is defined as a change in the net asset value of the fund combined with dividends and capital gains distributions.
Science and technology funds returned 5.62 percent. Lipper noted the sector has been able to recover from steep losses in the fourth quarter of 1995.

Michael Lipper, the president of the firm, said, however, he was cautious toward the sector, noting in a statement that the market is rewarding only selected issues rather than pushing all technology segments higher.
"I would buy where I thought there was proprietary value," he said. "This is not the time to be in commodity-type products."

Real estate funds also put in a strong performance, rising 5.75 percent in the quarter. Lipper said that strength in the sector "always raises the question of whether investors are worried about inflation, but the evidence is mixed."

One barometer, gold funds, fell 2.01 percent in the period, while another yardstick, natural resources funds, rose 4.09 percent. Growth funds rose 2.90 percent, mid-cap funds were up 3.24 percent, small company growth funds were up 1.75 percent, S&P 500 index funds increased 2.95 percent, growth and income funds were up 2.90 and equity income funds added 2.66 percent.
World equity funds underperformed their U.S. brethren, dropping 0.73 percent, and Japanese funds fell 6.37 percent.

Lipper said in the statement that about 30 percent of the drop in Japanese funds "can be blamed directly on a weaker yen; but much of the rest of the decline can be attributed to a pullback in Japanese equities, which levelled off after a strong recovery over the previous year or so."
Pacific funds, excluding Japan, fell 2.05 percent, and Latin American funds gained 1.29 percent.
Regarding U.S. equity funds, Lipper said that they are performing "well above historic norms."
He said for the first nine months, they rose 13.73 percent and over the last 12 months gained 16.90 percent.

He noted that over the last 35 years, general equity funds have returned an annualized average return of slightly less than 11 percent. "One would expect performance to pull back into that range," he said.

According to Lipper, the top five performers for the quarter were: Eaton Vance Marathon Gold & Natural Resources, up 19.60 percent; Insightful Investor Growth Fund, up 16.33 percent; Janus Equity Income, up 14.80 percent; Fidelity Export, up 14.11 percent; and GT Global Consumer Products Services Fund Class A, up 14.10 percent.

The bottom performers were: Pioneer India Class C, off 25.32 per cent; Pioneer India Class B, off 25.31 percent; Pioneer India Class A, off 25.03 percent; Frontier Equity Income, off 19.78 percent; Fidelity Selected Air Transportation, off 18.90 percent; Eaton Vance Marathon Greater India, off 18.74 percent; and Eaton Vance Traditional Greater India, off 18.59 percent.
